title: Odisha CM Orders Crime Branch Into Balianta Lynching
excerpt: CM Mohan Charan Majhi escalates probe after GRP constable Soumya Ranjan Swain killed by a mob of 40 near Bhubaneswar
body:
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on May 9 handed the Balianta lynching case to the Crime Branch, two days after a mob of roughly 40 people beat 32-year-old Government Railway Police constable Soumya Ranjan Swain to death on the outskirts of Bhubaneswar.

**What happened on May 7:**
Swain and his companion Om Prakash Rout collided with a scooter carrying two women near Ramachandrapur bridge in the Balianta area at around 11:30 am. The women alleged that Swain then attacked and attempted to rape one of them. Locals who heard the screams surrounded the two men and assaulted them; police arrived later and rushed both to hospital, where Swain was declared dead. Police have since registered two separate FIRs — one for attempted rape on the women's complaint, and a second for murder filed by Swain's family.

**Why the probe just got more complicated:**
Majhi ordered the Crime Branch escalation after chairing a high-level meeting, directing it to conduct 'a proper and thorough investigation' and take strict action against the culprits. The case carries a sharp political edge: Swain's father alleged that policemen on the scene also assaulted his son instead of rescuing him, a charge the government has neither confirmed nor dismissed. Opposition BJD chief Naveen Patnaik condemned the lynching and questioned the ruling BJP's management of law and order. Arrests have climbed to 11, with six suspects picked up on Saturday alone. A separate criminal case from 2021 and recent absences from duty add layers of complexity to Swain's profile.

**What to watch next:**
All eyes will be on whether the Crime Branch probe extends to the conduct of the police officers present at the scene — a finding that could turn a mob-violence case into a full-blown accountability crisis for the Majhi government.
